paras: The attempted lynching of John Smith took place at Waldron, Arkansas, on May 22, 1888, when a crowd took Smith, who was jailed on a charge of arson, from the jail twice and strung him up. Both times he was taken down alive when "cooler counsel prevailed" and was returned to jail. A short wire dispatch carried the story to papers as far off as Delaware, South Carolina, Georgia and Dakota Territory.

The residence of Rev. William McKay at Waldron was destroyed by fire on Tuesday, May 22. McKay's brother-in-law, John Smith, was arrested on a charge of setting the fire and was placed in jail. None of the reports gives Smith's race or any reason he was suspected.

According to the dispatch, "sentiment ran high" against Smith. The same day, "an excited crowd of citizens" took him from the jail and strung him up. The crowd let him down when calmer voices prevailed, then repeated the attempt, and again took him down and returned him to the jail. The reports do not mention the jailer, the sheriff or any other officer.
No report of arrests among the crowd, of a trial of Smith on the arson charge, or of his later fate was found in the coverage.

The episode reached the white press as a single brief dispatch datelined Waldron, May 23. The Wilmington Daily Republican printed it on May 24 under the headline "Twice Strung Up", and the Hand County Press of Miller, Dakota, ran it on May 31 as "Strung Up Twice by Lynchers". Neither paper added comment.

Southern papers shortened the story into filler. On May 30 the Yorkville Enquirer placed a rewritten version, with the minister's name spelled "Mackay", among its "Scraps and Facts", between a woman-suffrage ruling and the sale of a Black man for vagrancy in Missouri. The same day, the Savannah Morning News cut it to one sentence among its "Items of Interest", noting only that Smith was taken from jail twice by an excited crowd. None of the papers followed up on the story or commented on it.

reader.title: Attempted lynching of John Smith
bases: A crowd took an accused arsonist from jail and twice strung him up before letting him down and returning him to jail, an attempted lynching (A2, A5).
An 'excited crowd of citizens' with no lawful authority took Smith from jail over an arson charge and strung him up, but he was taken down alive and returned to jail, so no one was killed (A2, A5).

All four reports agree, but every one derives from a single Waldron dispatch of May 23, two printed as datelined wire copy (A2, A5) and two as rewritten briefs (A3, A4); no independent local account was found.

accounts.label: Wire report (Waldron, May 23)
accounts.gist: McKay's residence burned; his brother-in-law Smith was jailed for arson, taken out by an excited crowd and twice strung up, and taken down and returned to jail when cooler counsel prevailed.

framing.detail: The Daily Republican ran the dispatch as 'Twice Strung Up' and the Hand County Press as 'Strung Up Twice by Lynchers', both without comment.
The Yorkville Enquirer and Savannah Morning News reduced it to a filler item among miscellany ('Scraps and Facts', 'Items of Interest').

conflicts.note: A spelling variant only; the datelined wire copy reads McKay.
